newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-SANDBERG HOMERS TWICE AFTER ANNOUNCING RETIREMENT.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-SANDBERG HOMERS TWICE AFTER ANNOUNCING RETIREMENT.

text.p: No sooner had he announced his intention to retire at the end of the season, then future Hall of Famer Ryne Sandberg went out and ended the Cubs' nine-game losing steak.
Sandberg went 3-for-3 with a pair of homers on Saturday to lead the Chicago Cubs to a 5-1 win over Los Angeles that snapped the Dodgers' seven-game winning streak.
Prior to the game Sandberg, arguably baseball's all-time greatest second baseman, told a news conference that his 15th season with the Cubs would be his last.
But the announcement seemed premature after the 37-year-old produced one of his best games of the last two seasons, driving in three runs, scoring three times and stealing a base.
"It was pretty special watching Ryno do what he did today," said Cubs starter Kevin Tapani. "I guess anytime you get to share the field with a future Hall of Famer, it's pretty special."
Sandberg smacked a two-run homer off Tom Candiotti (7-4) in the second inning and belted a solo shot off Mark Guthrie in the third to put Chicago in front 3-1.
But the modest 10-time All-Star refused to take the credit for the victory. "It was just a total team effort today and a lot of fun to be out there," Sandberg said.
Tapani (2-1) allowed one run and eight hits over six innings. He also had a hit, drew a walk and stole his first major-league base.
In Houston, Mike Hampton pitched a three-hitter for his third career shutout and sixth straight win and Jeff Bagwell homered to lead the Astros to a 6-0 blanking of the New York Mets.
Hampton (9-7), who walked three and struck out seven, recorded his fifth complete game in seven starts. He is 7-0 in 11 starts at home this season.

Bagwell launched his 29th home run off Mets starter Bobby Jones (12-7) with two out in the first to give the Astros a 1-0 lead. They added four in the third on Derek Bell's two-run double RBI singles by Bill Spiers and Tim Bogar.
At Florida, Denny Neagle allowed four hits over seven scoreless innings and Kenny Lofton had two RBI to lead the Atlanta Braves to a 4-2 victory over the Marlins.
Neagle (15-2) ran his scoreless inning streak to 16 and walked two and struck out seven to join teammate Greg Maddux and Houston's Darryl Kile as the only 15-game winners in the National League.
Lofton had an RBI triple in the seventh to put the Braves up 3-0 and added an RBI single in the ninth as Atlanta halted the Marlins' four-game winning streak.
In Cincinnati, Eddie Taubensee, Willie Greene and Reggie Sanders all homered in support of rookie Brett Tomko as the Reds beat the San Francisco Giants 5-1.
Tomko (6-3) allowed a run and two hits with two walks and a career-high 10 strikeouts in seven innings before giving way to Jeff Shaw, who worked two perfect innings.
Mark Gardner (11-5) saw his three-game winning streak stopped. He gave up four runs -- three homers -- and seven hits in 5 1/3 innings.

In Montreal, Carlos Perez tossed a five-hitter for his fourth shutout of the season and Rondell White continued his torrid hitting with three hits, including a homer, as the Expos blanked the San Diego Padres 6-0.
Perez (11-6) allowed a double and four singles, walked two and struck out six in throwing 73 of 117 pitches for strikes en route to his ninth complete game.

White, who is 7-for-12 on the team's current homestand, hit a two-run homer off starter Pete Smith (4-2) in the fifth to stake Montreal to a 4-0 lead. David Segui followed with a solo shot for a five-run cushion.
In Philadelphia, Todd Stottlemyre scattered six hits over eight innings to outduel Matt Beech as the St Louis Cardinals edged the Phillies 2-1.
Stottlemyre (11-7) won for the seventh time in nine decisions and improved to 7-2 on the road as the Phillies saw their season-high four-game winning streak halted.
Beech (0-7) went six innings and gave up two runs and eight hits. He struck out eight but walked home the winning run with the bases loaded in the sixth as the Phils fell to 0-14 when Beech starts.

In Pittsburgh, Joe Randa had a two-run triple to highlight a five-run fifth inning and Francisco Cordova allowed one run over seven innings as the Pirates held on for a 6-5 win over the Colorado Rockies.

Cordova (8-6) allowed seven hits, including Larry Walker's league-leading 33rd homer. Relievers Marc Wilkins and Jason Christiansen struggled as the Rockies scored four times in the eighth before Rich Loiselle notched his 17th save.
Highly touted prospect Todd Helton homered in his major league debut for Colorado, which has lost four of six games. Walker went 3-for-4 to raise his average to .389.
